title: Passing once did not end the spell
era: 1994 Old School model using modern rules
matchup: Nested Draw Control against white-green creature midrange
story: I resolved Eureka with Mirror Universe and Sylvan Library in my hand. On my first opportunity I put Mirror Universe onto the battlefield. My opponent chose Serra Angel . I followed with Sylvan Library; my opponent declined their next opportunity. I passed on the next choice too, but we had not yet finished the spell just because one player had passed. When my opponent's turn to choose arrived again, they could still put another permanent from hand onto the battlefield. None of these permanents was cast; any enters-the-battlefield triggers waited until Eureka finished resolving.
review: Eureka alternates choices, does not end after one pass, cards are put onto battlefield rather than cast, triggers wait until resolution. Groundhog Day reference curated, opponent Serra Angel hypothetical. Historical date 1994 Old School style not claimed match.
claim: representative reconstruction; not a historical match or quotation
